clue.text: Diamonds hidden by one not wanting to leave what's left

indicators.note: diamonds are concealed within the voter, so that letter sits inside the longer word

parts.note: a Remainer is someone who voted for Britain to stay in the EU
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A Brexit-era pro-EU voter is sitting on a stash of gems, leaving others to wonder what is left over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden by' puts D inside REMAINER. A Remainer, in British politics, voted in 2016 for the UK to stay in the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest or residue of something is whatever is left over once a part is taken away.

clue.text: Makeshift neckwear by the sound of it

indicators.note: the clue asks us to hear the word for the neckwear spoken, then write a different spelling

parts.note: a ruff is a stiff pleated collar of the Elizabethan era

explanation.surface: Someone has improvised a scarf or collar, and it sounds like it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough-and-ready shelter or sketch is crude and improvised, done as a temporary stopgap.

clue.text: Philosopher's temper becomes a cross to bear

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was the philosopher, and the possessive adds the S
to temper or tone something is to moderate it, as in toning down

explanation.surface: A thinker's bad mood turns into a burden everyone around him must put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy, lasting burden or handicap is called a millstone round one's neck, as is a cross one has to bear.

clue.text: It's including inaccurate centres as crosses

indicators.note: the first word wraps around the scrambled word, taking it inside

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving the letters as written

indicators.note: inaccurate means not correct, so these letters are out of their proper order

explanation.surface: Someone complains that mismeasured midpoints make lines meet where they should not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' looks like the start of a sentence but supplies letters; 'inaccurate' makes NTERSEC, which 'including' places within.
explanation.definitionFit: When two roads or lines cross they meet and pass through each other at a point.

clue.text: Play about dalliance with girl

indicators.note: with lets the girl's name join the other word, here at its front

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, from Diana
sport in the old sense of amorous play or flirtation

explanation.surface: Someone flirting idly with a young woman is told to stop messing around.
explanation.definitionFit: To frolic or amuse oneself in a lively, carefree way is to romp and play around.

clue.text: Copy both sides of reverse fold

indicators.note: only the two end letters of the word are taken, one from each side

parts.note: a plica is an anatomical fold of skin or membrane

explanation.surface: Instructions for duplicating a sheet: crease it back on itself on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is a faithful reproduction or duplicate made of an original.

clue.text: Occurs in spades after autumn

indicators.note: the card suit comes after the season in the answer

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Something happens in great abundance once autumn has arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: When a date or event falls on a day, it happens or takes place then.

clue.text: Set up animal run

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a wolf is the wild canine animal

explanation.surface: A creature has been framed and decides to flee.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that runs moves steadily along in a stream, as liquid does when it pours.

clue.text: Turner's state of excitement cut short

definitions.note: read as Turner is, the 's joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter, docked at the tail

parts.note: to be in a lather is to be agitated and worked up

explanation.surface: J. M. W. Turner, the painter, works himself up into a frenzy that is quickly cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner is the painter in the surface but a woodworker's machine in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodturning machine spins the workpiece so it can be shaped, the classic tool of the trade.

clue.text: Lie about returning after spell in prison

indicators.note: the reversed letters follow the jail term in the answer

parts.note: a stretch is slang for a prison sentence

indicators.note: returning means the two-letter word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: An ex-prisoner fibs about coming back after doing time.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher is old slang for an exaggeration or tall tale, a falsehood that stretches the truth.

clue.text: One left on board not having been ignited

indicators.note: a passenger on board is inside the vessel, so the letter goes inside the word

parts.note: a unit is a single thing, one

explanation.surface: A single passenger left aboard a ship that never fired its engines.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire, candle or lamp that has not been set alight remains dark, never kindled.

clue.text: Exceptionally fine wine drunk in a second

indicators.note: the wine is swallowed, taken inside the other word

parts.note: super means excellent, exceptionally fine
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A top-notch wine is knocked back in a single moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A second in a duel or boxing match is the person who backs and assists a principal.

clue.text: Affected by trichinosis — almost collapsing

indicators.note: the remaining letters fall apart and are rebuilt in a new order
almost the whole word is used, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A patient suffering from a parasitic worm infection is close to keeling over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TRICHINOSIS to TRICHINOSI, which 'collapsing' rearranges. Trichinosis is a disease caught from undercooked pork.
explanation.definitionFit: Histrionic behaviour is theatrical and exaggerated, putting on airs in an unnatural, mannered way.

clue.text: Opening of medical facility near the centre of Malvern

indicators.note: the hospital department sits beside the single letter, after it
only the middle letter of the town's name is taken

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A new clinic is opening close to the middle of Malvern, a spa town in Worcestershire, England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' reads as a launch, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vent is an aperture or outlet that lets air, gas or smoke escape.

clue.text: About to review stories by Malawi's principal educator

indicators.note: the letter stands beside the rest, at its start
principal means first, so the opening letter is taken

parts.note: on means about, concerning, as in a talk on art

indicators.note: to review is to go over and rework, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A headteacher in Malawi is about to look over some tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review' rearranges STORIES as TESSORI. Maria Montessori was the Italian educator whose teaching method bears her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria Montessori was a pioneering Italian teacher who founded a famous child-centred method of schooling.

clue.text: Object expert needs to examine

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
to test is to examine or check

explanation.surface: A specialist is needed to inspect some item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' reads as a noun, a thing to examine, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To object is to complain or raise a formal objection, voicing disapproval.

clue.text: Job to detest? Describing the bottom of Mistress Quickly

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: describing in its old sense of drawing around, so the word encircles the letter

parts.note: to hate is to detest

indicators.note: the bottom of the word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Mistress Quickly, Shakespeare's tavern hostess, has a job she loathes, with a cheeky aside on her backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Done with all possible speed, in great haste, as a messenger riding hard.

clue.text: A refusal by university hospital to admit the Italian dramatist

indicators.note: the run of pieces lets the Italian article in, holding it inside

parts.note: no is a refusal
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
il is the Italian word for the

explanation.surface: A university hospital turns away a playwright from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean Anouilh was a French playwright, author of Antigone; 'the Italian' only supplies IL.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Anouilh was a twentieth-century French playwright, so he is a writer of plays.

clue.text: Lines feeding one kind of malevolence

indicators.note: the lines feed in after the numeral, joining on behind it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
L is short for line, so LL is lines
nature means kind or sort, as in things of that nature

explanation.surface: Queues are being fed into a single variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite and a bad temper are signs of a mean, unkind disposition.

clue.text: Idea Tory dismissed sharing thus becoming a doubter

indicators.note: the word for thus splits to share its space with the rest, which goes inside

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quoted error

indicators.note: the party member is sent away, taken out of the longer word

parts.note: a concept is an idea
Con is short for Conservative, a member of the Tory party

explanation.surface: A Conservative's notion is rejected, and those sharing it end up having doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: Con is short for Conservative; 'dismissed' leaves CEPT, and 'sharing' has the Latin word split around it. Sic is what editors print beside a quoted error.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic questions accepted claims and needs convincing, unwilling to believe without proof.

clue.text: Require company employee to live in Maryland

indicators.note: the worker lives within the state, so the word goes inside its abbreviation

parts.note: MD is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maryland
a man is a worker or employee, as in management and men

explanation.surface: A firm insists that a staff member must relocate to Maryland.
explanation.definitionFit: To command something is to order or demand it, insisting it be done.

clue.text: Poins, for instance, taking in the opening of Lancaster's decisive argument

indicators.note: the compiler takes the letter inside

parts.note: Poins is the pseudonym of this puzzle's compiler, an example of a crossword setter

indicators.note: the opening of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Poins, Prince Hal's companion in Shakespeare's Henry IV, joins in as the House of Lancaster wins a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: Poins is both the Shakespeare character in the surface and the setter of this crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler is an informal word for a remark or blow that ends a dispute once and for all.

clue.text: Learned about pipe lengths originally required on Snetzler's earliest organs

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another goes after it
the word goes around the two letters, enclosing them

parts.note: seen as in found out: having seen something you have learned it

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of each of the two words
the earliest letter of the name is its first

explanation.surface: An expert on the lengths of pipes for the first instruments built by Snetzler, an eighteenth-century organ maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organs' looks like the pipe organs of the surface but means body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The spleen is an abdominal organ that filters blood, so several of them are bodily organs.

clue.text: Composer essentially disregarded by a great many people

indicators.note: the essential middle letter of the name is ignored and removed

parts.note: Gustav Holst was the English composer of The Planets

explanation.surface: A composer is mostly overlooked by large numbers of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a large crowd or multitude, as in a host of admirers.

clue.text: Sons standing by Heather for support

indicators.note: the letter stands next to the plant name, before it

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
ling is a name for common heather

explanation.surface: Her sons stand loyally beside Heather, giving her their support.
explanation.definitionFit: A sling is a supportive bandage that holds up an injured arm.

clue.text: Places without parking designed to accommodate sheltered walks of limited size

indicators.note: the rearranged letters house the walks inside them
the remaining letters are designed afresh, arranged in a new order
the parking letter is left out of the word

parts.note: P is the road-sign symbol for parking
a mall is a covered shopping walkway

explanation.surface: Town planners lay out spots with no car parking, built around covered shopping arcades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops P from PLACES, and 'designed' rearranges LACES as SCALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-scale describes an enterprise or project that is modest in extent and scope.

clue.text: Be without at first

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
1st written with I standing for the figure 1

explanation.surface: An instruction to go without, at least at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the sense of having being, being real and alive.

clue.text: Reflect in silence as first of birds goes south

indicators.note: it is the leading letter of the word that is moved
in a down clue going south is going down to the bottom, the end

parts.note: emus are large flightless Australian birds

explanation.surface: Someone thinks quietly as the first bird heads south for winter.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder or meditate quietly, lost in thought.

clue.text: Guarantee from uranium mines in recession recently

indicators.note: receding means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium
pits are mines
late means recently, as in of late

explanation.surface: A promise wrung from uranium mining firms that have lately fallen into economic decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recession' looks economic but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To stipulate is to specify or demand something as a condition of an agreement, securing it.

clue.text: Abandoned oil cans made mostly into circular designs

indicators.note: a can contains, so the scrambled letters hold the rest
abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so these letters run loose in a new order
most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to cut a record is to make one

explanation.surface: Discarded oil drums are mostly turned into round patterns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' gives OLI and 'mostly' gives CU; 'cans' means contains, not tins. Oculi is the Latin plural of oculus, an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: An oculus is a round window or eye-like ornament in architecture, so several are round motifs.

clue.text: Dog bowl initially ignored by bird

indicators.note: the letter is ignored, left out of the dog's name

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of hound

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A hungry dog's food dish goes unnoticed by a bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is a large bird of prey with a hooked beak and keen eyesight.

clue.text: Criticise position on books in opposition to official policy

parts.note: to dis or diss is slang for to disparage or criticise
a side is a position taken in an argument
NT is the New Testament, the books of the Christian Bible after the Old

explanation.surface: Someone attacks the stance taken on reading material, against the official line.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissident position challenges established doctrine or state authority, rebelling against it.
